builds.name: Reference: Ranked mid core
builds.goal: Reference for Lissandra: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ mid players use most (7,662 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 53% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A close-range control mage who uses claw repositioning to enter, lock targets and turn nearby deaths into follow-up threats. The current mid provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Malignance → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass. Electrocute keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Sorcerer's Shoes, Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff.
builds.summary: The proven mid baseline: Malignance → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass, with Electrocute.
testPlan: Play it in mid as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Malignance → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 53% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Malignance → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

kitEvidence.formula: Lissandra creates an ice field, Rooting nearby enemies for [1.25 / 1.35 / 1.45 / 1.55 / 1.65] seconds and dealing [70 / 105 / 140 / 175 / 210 + (0.7) × AP] magic damage.

Lissandra encases herself or an enemy champion in ice. Enemies are Stunned for [1.5] seconds. When self cast, Lissandra enters Stasis for [2.5] seconds and restores [100 / 150 / 200 + (0.55) × AP] Health, increased by [1]% for each [1]% missing Health.

In either case, dark ice eminates from the target, dealing [150 / 250 / 350 + (0.75) × AP] magic damage. The ice persists for [3] seconds, Slowing enemies by [(-0.45 / -0.6 / -0.75) × -100]%.
Lissandra casts forth an ice claw that deals [70 / 105 / 140 / 175 / 210 + (0.6) × AP] magic damage. Lissandra can Recast while the claw travels to teleport to its location.

Lissandra throws a spear of ice that shatters on the first enemy hit, dealing [80 / 115 / 150 / 185 / 220 + (0.75) × AP] magic damage, Slowing them by [(-0.2 / -0.24 / -0.28 / -0.32 / -0.36) × -100]% for [1.5] seconds, and also damaging and slowing the enemies behind them.

When an enemy champion dies near Lissandra they become a frozen zombie that seeks out living enemies. Enemies near these zombies are Slowed by [25]%. After [4] seconds, frozen zombies shatter, dealing [characterLevelBreakpoints(start=120, perLevel=20, changes=[{"mLevel": 13, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": 30.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}]) + (0.5) × AP] magic damage.

builds.name: Tomb drain frontliner
builds.summary: Use self-Tomb as a timed healing pivot inside sustained combat.
builds.goal: Use self-Tomb as a timed healing pivot inside sustained combat.
builds.hypothesis: Self-cast Frozen Tomb creates 2.5 seconds of stasis and an AP heal increased with missing health; it still emits magic dark ice. Rod and Riftmaker support health/AP, Visage enhances received healing and Abyssal serves close magic contact. Ring of Frost and E access create the entry, while Zhonya's can extend safety if used as a separate planned window.
testPlan: Required state: Need self R ready, nearby enemies held and missing health without lethal pre-cast damage.
Compare healing, damage and escape after a W-self-R sequence at two starting health values.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Stasis alone does not protect allies; enemies can wait beyond the ice and punish the exit.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Enemy-cast Tomb supplies stun rather than the documented self heal/stasis package.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Rod of Ages, Riftmaker, Spirit Visage, Zhonya's Hourglass, Abyssal Mask, Mercury's Treads. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Survive the engage
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Lissandra: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A close-range control mage who uses claw repositioning to enter, lock targets and turn nearby deaths into follow-up threats. Measure claw entry, self-R versus enemy R and passive thrall follow-up. A support tank route trades AP for reliable control; no simultaneous offensive and defensive R. A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
builds.summary: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
testPlan: Kit question for Lissandra: Measure claw entry, self-R versus enemy R and passive thrall follow-up. A support tank route trades AP for reliable control; no simultaneous offensive and defensive R.

Start with the early core (Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Throws a spear of ice that shatters when it hits an enemy, dealing magic damage and slowing Move Speed. Shards pass through the target, dealing the same damage to other enemies hit. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.

The route fails Lissandra's stated kit question: Measure claw entry, self-R versus enemy R and passive thrall follow-up. A support tank route trades AP for reliable control; no simultaneous offensive and defensive R.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.
Full cost 16,000 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Banshee's Veil, Rylai's Crystal Scepter, Void Staff are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Frozen zombie chain finisher
builds.summary: Seek a first death that turns into delayed area cleanup.
builds.goal: Seek a first death that turns into delayed area cleanup.
builds.hypothesis: Iceborn Subjugation creates zombies on nearby champion deaths; they slow, then shatter after four seconds for level damage plus 0.5 AP magic. Shadowflame can improve low-health magic hits and Cryptbloom adds a heal nova on qualifying deaths. Malignance supplies R pressure for the initial victim, with high AP retaining the delayed zombie threat.
testPlan: Required state: Need a genuine nearby death and living enemies still close when the zombie shatters.
Measure first-victim burst and zombie damage separately, including failed chain cases with enemy disengage.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: No first death means no passive damage; surviving enemies spread before the delay expires.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Zombies are not normal attacking pets and cannot be assigned owner attack on-hits without evidence.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Luden's Echo, Shadowflame, Rabadon's Deathcap, Cryptbloom, Malignance, Sorcerer's Shoes. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
